11.657.why: dīa is two syllables (dī-ă, from dīus), and decus is long by position before sibi: Ī-tă-lĭ | dēs quās | ip-să dĕ | cūs sĭ-bĭ | dī-ă Că | mil-la (16 syllables), caesura after decus. The scanner (cost 1.5, not flagged) ran dia into one syllable, counted 15 and made both syllables of sibi long to fit.

11.659.why: Confirmed by hand, entered only to clear the COSTLY flag: Thrēĭcĭae is four syllables (Greek Θρηΐκιος; Greenough prints Threïcius at 6.645) and the Greek name Thermōdōn (ω) gives a spondaic fifth foot: quā-lēs | Thrē-ĭ-cĭ | ae cum | flū-mĭ-nă | Thēr-mō | dōn-tis (14 syllables), caesura after Threiciae. The scanner's parse was right; the cost is the spondaic fifth foot.

11.662.why: Penthĕsĭlēa is five syllables (Greek Πενθεσίλεια, -lē-ă, as Penthesilea furens at 1.491), and rĕfert has a short re-: Pen-thĕ-sĭ | lē-ă rĕ | fert mag | nōqu(e) ŭ-lŭ | lān-tĕ tŭ | mul-tu (16 syllables), magnoque elided into ululante, caesura after refert. The scanner (cost 1.5, not flagged) ran -lea into one syllable, counted 15 and lengthened re- to fit.

11.665.why: dēĭcis is three syllables (dē-ĭ-cis: de + iacio, dē- long), and its -cĭs is short before the vowel of Aut; quŏt is short before humi (h makes no position): dē-ĭ-cĭs | aut quŏt hŭ | mī mŏ-rĭ | en-tĭ-ă | cor-pŏ-ră | fun-dis (17 syllables, five dactyls), caesura after humi. The scanner (cost 1.5, not flagged) read dei- as one syllable, counted 16 and made -cis long.

11.678.why: Ĭāpyx is a Greek name (Ἰᾶπυξ) with a vowel I, so Iapyge is four syllables, Ĭ-ā-pў-gĕ (as Iapyge at 8.710 and Iapyx at 12.391), and vēnātŏr keeps its short -or before it: ig-nō | tīs ĕt ĕ | quō vē | nā-tŏr Ĭ | ā-pў-gĕ | fer-tur (15 syllables), caesura after equo. The scanner (cost 0.0, not flagged) read Ia- as consonantal (Ja-), counted 14 and lengthened -tor.
